A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BrepCoder research. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v3 additionally contains readable supplementary Sections A–B.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 and Tables 1–3 report original BrepCoder experiments on reverse engineering, completion, error correction and CAD-QA, including ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original task evaluations and adds comparison results, ablations, visual-quality scores and supplementary qualitative results.

M1.justification: The proposed UV-Net/CoCa alignment, losses, frozen encoder, three-layer projector and two-stage LLM training remain unchanged. Added encoder and backbone variants are ablations. v3 explicitly specifies scratch initialization, but v1 does not specify initialization sufficiently to establish a changed core procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use DeepCAD for reverse engineering, completion and error correction, and SGP-Bench for CAD-QA. The appendix supplies further examples within this coverage, without adding datasets, task requirements or distinct test environments.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds retrained, B-rep-conditioned DeepCAD and Brep2Seq comparators for both completion and error correction, substantially strengthening comparisons with matching inputs. Completion removes GPT-4, GPT-3.5, LLaMA3 and Mistral while retaining CAD-Llama. Table 1 removes MultiCAD and View2CAD; the CAD-QA comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds GPT-5 visual assessment of isometric renders against ground truth on a 0–5 scale, alongside settings for new baseline controls and encoder/backbone ablations. Existing splits, masking and corruption ranges, and 8,096-point Chamfer-distance evaluation remain unchanged. Appendix A's training budgets are newly disclosed, rather than established revisions to earlier settings.

E4.justification: Table 3(a) adds tests of omitting Phase 1 alignment, segmentation-pretrained encoder initialization, replacing UV-Net with AAGNet, and using Llama-3.2 1B. These examine previously untested dependencies of the approach. Supplementary Section B.1 also adds command-count and command-order ambiguity cases with accompanying accuracy and distance values.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. The added experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The headline reverse-engineering ACCcmd/ACCparam/CD changes from 89.39/81.93/0.499 to 89.34/82.01/0.464. The earlier tuple reappears under Pre-trained Encoder, so this is not an established same-setting gain. v3 adds substantial baseline, ablation, VLM-score and qualitative results, plus completion CD/IR entries. Table 3(b)'s error-correction invalid-ratio ranking reverses; CAD-QA accuracies remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same feature mappings, losses and accuracy definitions, apart from punctuation and formatting. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a unified B-rep-based MLLM, code alignment and two-stage training supporting four CAD tasks. Additional experimental support does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving segmentation-pretraining bias and AAGNet's coarser UV sampling, and interprets the Llama experiment as backbone robustness. Supplementary Section B.1 further interprets alternative command sequences as evidence against memorization. These extend the existing mechanism discussion without substantially changing its overall scope or adding a substantive limitations analysis.

D1.justification: v1 provides little implementation information beyond the backbone and decoder depth. New Appendix A documents four H100 GPUs, tokenization, contrastive temperature, AdamW learning rates, scheduling, dropout, epochs, batch sizes, DeepSpeed configurations, projector dimensions and validation-based checkpoint selection. Appendix B also identifies OpenCASCADE for visualization. These are substantial reproducibility disclosures.

R1.justification: v3 adds the AAGNet reference and removes Mistral 7B, Ouyang et al.'s instruction-following paper and the original LLaMA reference. The related-work narrative and positioning against task-specific CAD models and BrepLLM remain substantially unchanged. Most other bibliography edits add metadata or DOI links.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. v3 tightens method and downstream-task explanations, explicitly labels the two phases in subsection headings, standardizes terminology, fixes the running title, updates contact details and adds acknowledgements and organized supplementary sections.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a VLM column and moves; Table 2 merges completion and error correction into a larger shared display; Table 3 expands its ablation rows. Eight supplementary figures substantially extend the visual presentation with ambiguity analyses and task examples, including some reused reverse-engineering examples. The main framework figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses two weaknesses of v1: downstream comparisons confounded by input modality and sparse training documentation. B-rep-conditioned baselines in Table 2, stronger component controls in Table 3 and Appendix A's training recipe make the central contribution more assessable and reproducible. Removed comparators narrow comparison breadth, and uncertainty reporting remains absent; the 92.69 versus 92.96 completion-accuracy discrepancy also persists. Nevertheless, the improved controls and documentation provide a clear substantial net gain.
